title: Quantile interleaving field log — microburst sampling
content:
Goal:
Quick, lightweight field notes from a small series of runs that tried a "quantile-interleaving" sampling approach to detect transient microbursts and measure tail mass without full-trace capture. This is a personal scratchpad — not a formal writeup.

Hypothesis:
Interleaving different quantile sampling windows (short high-frequency sampling + periodic longer-window snapshots) will reveal short-lived p99+ excursions that uniform sampling misses, while keeping storage/ingest overhead low.

Harness / setup:
- Cluster: dev-gpu-pool-07 (4x A10G) behind local proxy.
- Workload: synthetic T2 prompt mix (50/30/20 short/medium/long).
- Baseline qps: 80 steady, then impulse blasts to 400 qps for 10s every 3 minutes.
- Duration: 6h run (2025-02-11 09:00–15:00 PST).
- Instrumentation: local client emits per-request latency, token-count, model variant. Collector aggregates to 5s bins; additional high-frequency sampler records 100ms bins but only for 1 of every 30s windows (interleaved).

Sampling design (quantile-interleaving):
- Short window sampler: 100ms bins for 10s, triggered every 30s (captures microbursts)
- Long window sampler: 5s bins continuous (for steady-state)
- Disk footprint: ~1.2GB for 6h run (vs 8.7GB full-trace)

Key observations:
1) Burst detection: short-window sampler found 3 distinct p99+ spikes during scheduled impulses that 5s bins blurred into p95-range. The 100ms resolution showed spikes concentrated in the first 2s of the blast.
2) Spike morphology: each spike had a steep rise (~120ms to peak) and exponential decay ~800–1200ms. Suggests queueing + short-lived GC/wakeup synergy.
3) Interleaving cadence matters: when short-window sampling alignment missed the first 30s boundary (client jitter), one of the spike families was only partially captured. Need randomized phase shift.
4) Token-length correlation: long prompts contributed disproportionately to prolonged tails (single long request could produce 60–120ms added tail). But majority of p99 mass in blasts came from short requests hitting queueing simultaneously.

Representative ascii sketch (p99 by time window):
[09:03] 5s-bin: 46ms | 100ms-sample: 46,48,47,46,140,180,170,55,48,47
[09:06] 5s-bin: 52ms | 100ms-sample: 52,53,51,49,50,49,48,47,46,50
[09:09] 5s-bin: 49ms | 100ms-sample: 49,140,190,210,180,60,50,48,47,46

Quick numbers (approx):
- 5s-bin p99 overall: 180ms (over 6h)
- 100ms-sample peak p99 during blasts: 410ms
- Rate of detectable microbursts (per hour): 6 with scheduled blasts, 2 spontaneous

Actions / next experiments:
- Add randomized phase offset for short-window sampler (0..30s) to reduce alignment miss.
- Try adding a 50ms bin sampler for the first 3s of blasts to see sub-100ms structure.
- Re-run with varying client shaping (e.g., ramp vs. instant blast) to measure sensitivity.
- Correlate with host-level traces (sched latency, CPU steal, GPU driver wakeups) — open a short sampling window for these metrics at the same interleaving cadence.

Notes / loose thoughts:
- This method is promising for production telemetry where full tracing is too expensive. Might be a candidate for a feature in Console's sampling recommendations (Reduce ingest, keep burst visibility).
- Need to define failure modes: if bursts are shorter than the short-window period, we'll miss them. Consider event-driven triggers (on RTT increase) to spawn immediate high-res sampling.

Open questions:
- What minimal short-window duty-cycle captures >90% of blasts across different infra? (tradeoff: resolution vs footprint)
- How much of the p99 mass is deterministic (client batching) vs stochastic infra events?

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Implement randomized short-window phase and re-run (Riley)
- [ ] Wire host-level wakeup counters into same sampler (Arjun)
- [ ] Draft a short one-pager for product (if repeatable) about sampled microburst detection

Quick links to raw artifacts: see linked_artifacts list above.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to a small internal note if next runs are consistent.
